subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 23, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - August 23, 2026

Development continues at a steady pace as our team refines the core AcreetionOS experience. Natalie pushed a new bash2bat conversion script to GitLab this week, expanding our cross-platform tooling for users who need Windows compatibility. Darren has been hard at work on the Calamares installer customization, ensuring smooth first-boot experiences for new users. The ISO build pipeline received several reliability improvements through deploy key fixes across multiple repositories.

Our GitLab infrastructure saw important security hardening with secret detection now configured in CI pipelines. The team re-triggered mirror synchronization across the acreetionos-archiso, acreetionos-news-tracker, and acreetion-appstore projects after resolving deploy key issues. These backend improvements strengthen our supply chain security and ensure reliable artifact delivery. Natalie also updated her personal bash2bat repository with the same secret detection workflow.

Upstream security updates from major distributions landed this week and are being evaluated for inclusion. AlmaLinux issued patches for ansible-core and pcp, while Debian updated chromium, libgit2, python-httplib2, and sabnzbdplus. Fedora also released several security advisories that our maintainers are reviewing. KDE Gear 26.08 arrived with its usual suite of application improvements and bug fixes.

Community engagement remains strong on our Discord server and social channels. New users continue to discover AcreetionOS through word-of-mouth recommendations about our privacy-first approach. The father-daughter development dynamic continues to resonate with community members who appreciate the personal touch. Darren's candid updates about infrastructure work and gaming adventures add authentic flavor to our project communications.

Our GitLab instance at gitlab.acreetionos.org serves as the primary collaboration hub for contributors. Both Natalie and Darren maintain active profiles there with project tracking and issue management. The instance admin message directs support requests to Discord, keeping communication channels organized. New contributors can find onboarding documentation in the project wikis.

The project website at acreetionos.org continues to serve as the central entry point for downloads and documentation. The FAQ page addresses common questions about project leadership, installation requirements, and design philosophy. Version 1.0 remains the current stable release with Cinnamon desktop and XLibre graphics stack. System requirements stay modest at 2GB RAM minimum and 20GB storage.

Tip of the week: Use the flash.html utility on our website for creating bootable USB drives with proper EFI support. This tool handles the tricky parts of UEFI boot preparation automatically. Verify your download checksums before flashing to ensure media integrity. The Cinnamon desktop includes a built-in screenshot tool accessible via Print Screen key for quick captures.

Highlight: Repository sovereignty means you control your software sources without forced telemetry or corporate mirrors. Our package repositories are hosted on infrastructure we own and operate. This design choice aligns with our privacy-first mission and prevents third-party tracking. Users can audit every connection their system makes to our update servers.

Reminder: Join our Discord at discord.gg/VHqQkJASw7 for real-time support and community discussion. Follow @acreetionos on X and Bluesky for announcements and development snapshots. The project thrives on community feedback — report issues, suggest features, or just say hello. Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS journey.
